narration.title: One company's books
narration.text: The roastery's [trial balance]: every account's year-end balance, built from entries with a [debit] and a [credit] side. One purchase, a burner igniter, sits in the wrong account.

data.title: Here today
data.text: The 214.77 igniter is part of this account's balance.

host.why: A cost in the wrong account makes both accounts wrong, and the reports built on them.

narration.title: The change lives in a manifest
narration.text: A [manifest] collects proposed changes so they can be read and checked first. This one, **fix-igniter**, holds one entry.

host.why: Nothing here touches the books until the owner approves.

narration.title: Before and after
narration.text: Opening the entry shows the document as it is and as it would be. Only the account on the line changes: **6140 → 6310**. The amount, the date and the supplier stay the same.

host.why: A change you can see side by side is a change you can check.

narration.title: Why it can't just be edited
narration.text: This card payment is [reconciled]: it was matched to the real bank statement. Xero refuses to let software edit a reconciled transaction, so the check stopped this entry until a way round was chosen.

data.title: On a reconciled payment
data.text: Matched to the statement, so Xero won't take an edit.

host.why: The statement match is what proves a payment happened; it isn't undone to fix a code.

narration.title: The way round: a reclass journal
narration.text: Instead of editing the payment, a [reclass journal] moves the amount: a [debit] to the right account and a [credit] to the wrong one, dated like the payment. The payment itself stays exactly as reconciled.

narration.title: The check
narration.text: Every entry goes through the [check] before anything else: journals must balance, accounts must exist, nothing may touch a closed period the wrong way. With the reclass chosen, there are no issues left.

data.text: The check mark: no issues left.

narration.title: Planned: sealed in a package
narration.text: The checked manifest was turned into the exact requests that would be sent, and sealed with a hash: the [plan]. The stage strip shows where it is: planned, waiting for approval.

narration.title: Approve, then apply, from your own terminal
narration.text: The owner [approve]s the package by its hash, then runs [apply]. Both commands are shown here; `y` copies the full command. No agent and no walkthrough can run them.

data.title: Your commands
data.text: Copy them with y and run them yourself.

host.why: Approval names the exact package: anything changed afterwards needs a new approval.

narration.title: After apply
narration.text: Apply sends the journal, then reads it back from Xero. The entry shows as posted only when the read-back matches the plan. The trial balance then moves 214.77 from 6140 to 6310.

data.title: Where it lands
data.text: After apply, the 214.77 is part of this balance.

host.why: Read-back is how you know the books say what was approved.

narration.title: The account, as a T
narration.text: Accountants draw an account as a T: [debit]s on the left, [credit]s on the right, the balance at the bottom. This is account 6140 today, with the igniter among its debits. After apply, a credit of 214.77 joins the right side and the balance drops by the same.

host.why: Every balance is just its debits less its credits; the T shows which entries make it.
